# MUSE — Continuous Development with Codex and Claude Code

> MUSE 3.6 preserves roles, decisions and next steps in shared project records.

MUSE combines Markdown skills and workflows with a Python continuity runtime.
Use Codex alone, Claude Code alone, or move the same role and Lane between them.
A Lane is a workstream with its own checkpoint; the agent derives goals,
constraints and acceptance checks from the user's request and recorded evidence.

## Daily use

- Continue an active conversation with a normal request such as "continue".
- `/resume strategy Lane A`: review and recover the chosen role and Lane.
- `/save`: persist useful progress without ending the conversation.
- `/bye`: perform an explicit formal closeout for a declared scope.
- Context pressure: save, compact when supported, verify the state, then continue.
  A percentage does not force Bye or a new conversation. Unknown usage stays unknown.

Projects retain their own division of work. Strategy can implement directly;
starting technical work or changing clients does not automatically switch to Build.
Existing closed Lanes retain their reopen conditions. Missing old Lane records
must be investigated, not silently initialized as empty.

## Switching clients

Save and stop the active writer, then resume the same role and Lane in the other
client. The receiving agent reviews the workspace, decisions and evidence gaps
before taking over. MUSE helpers reject saves from a previous writer after a
claim. Parallel work needs distinct scopes and isolated workspaces; arbitrary
external file edits are outside these helper protections.

## Install or upgrade

Requires Git, Python 3.7+ and a local macOS/Linux filesystem. Use a client version
that supports the selected model. From the directory containing the cloned repo:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/myths-labs/muse.git
bash muse/scripts/install.sh --tool codex --target /path/to/project
bash muse/scripts/install.sh --tool claude --target /path/to/project
```

Install only the client you use, or point both at the same project. User policy
and existing Claude hooks are preserved. Known 3.5 workflows are backed up;
unknown local modifications stop installation for review. Installation does not
create or claim a Lane. Keep installation/rollback receipts private.

## Package and compatibility

- 66 skills: Core 8, Toolkit 44, Ecosystem 13, Growth distribution 1.
- Guarded native continuity: Codex and Claude Code.
- Existing skill adapters: Claude Code, OpenClaw, OpenCode, Cursor, Windsurf,
  Gemini CLI, Codex, Copilot, Aider, Antigravity. Adapter support does not imply
  equivalent native continuity certification.
- Optional project dashboard, directive workflows and long-term notes.
- MIT license. No hosted MUSE service is required for the local continuity runtime.

## Verification boundaries

The 3.6 release has 44 public installer/state regressions passing on Linux and
macOS, plus a separate native Codex → Claude Code → Codex exercise. Synthetic
fixtures are not native evidence. Missing source coverage stays incomplete;
Save, Bye and automatic compaction do not guarantee lossless memory or product
readiness. Native Windows and network filesystem durability are not certified.
